{{Short description|Undirected graph with no non-trivial symmetries}}
[[Image:Asym-graph.PNG|thumb|250px|The eight 6-vertex asymmetric graphs]]
[[File:Frucht graph.dot.svg|thumb|The [[Frucht graph]], one of the five smallest asymmetric [[cubic graph|cubic graphs]].]]
{{Graph families defined by their automorphisms}}

In [[graph theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], an [[undirected graph]] is called an '''asymmetric graph''' if it has no nontrivial [[graph automorphism|symmetries]].

Formally, an [[graph automorphism|automorphism]] of a graph is a [[permutation]] {{mvar|p}} of its [[Vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] with the property that any two vertices {{mvar|u}} and {{mvar|v}} are adjacent [[if and only if]] {{math|''p''(''u'')}} and {{math|''p''(''v'')}} are adjacent.
The [[identity mapping]] of a graph is always an automorphism, and is called the  [[trivial automorphism]] of the graph. An asymmetric graph is a graph for which there are no other automorphisms.

Note that the term "asymmetric graph" is not a negation of the term "[[symmetric graph]]," as the latter refers to a stronger condition than possessing nontrivial symmetries.

==Examples==
The smallest asymmetric [[trivial graph|non-trivial]] graphs have 6 vertices.<ref name="er63"/> The smallest asymmetric [[regular graph]]s have ten vertices; there exist {{nowrap|10-vertex}} asymmetric graphs that are {{nowrap|4-regular}} and {{nowrap|5-regular}}.<ref>{{citation

 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation

 | journal = Universidad Técnica Federico Santa Maria. Scientia
 | pages = 103–111

J.|publisher=Dept. of Mathematics and Computing Science, Eindhoven University of Technology|series=EUT report|title=Computer investigation of cubic graphs|url=https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/computer-investigation-of-cubic-graphs|volume=76-WSK-01|year=1976}}</ref> is the twelve-vertex [[Frucht graph]] discovered in 1939.<ref name="f39">{{Citation | last1=Frucht | first1=R. | authorlink = Robert Frucht | title=Herstellung von Graphen mit vorgegebener abstrakter Gruppe. | url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=CM_1939__6__239_0 | language=German | zbl=0020.07804 | year=1939 | journal=Compositio Mathematica | issn=0010-437X | volume=6 | pages=239–250}}.</ref> According to a strengthened version of [[Frucht's theorem]], there are infinitely many asymmetric cubic graphs.

==Properties==
The class of asymmetric graphs is closed under [[complement graph|complements]]: a graph ''G'' is asymmetric if and only if its complement is.<ref name="er63"/> Any ''n''-vertex asymmetric graph can be made symmetric by adding and removing a total of at most ''n''/2&nbsp;+&nbsp;o(''n'') edges.<ref name="er63"/>

==Random graphs==
The proportion of graphs on ''n'' vertices with a nontrivial automorphism tends to zero as ''n'' grows, which is informally expressed as "[[almost all]] finite graphs are asymmetric".  In contrast, again informally, "almost all infinite graphs have nontrivial symmetries." More specifically, [[countable|countably]] infinite [[random graph]]s in the [[Erdős–Rényi model]] are, with [[probability 1]], [[graph isomorphism|isomorphic]] to the highly symmetric [[Rado graph]].<ref name="er63">{{citation|first1=P.|last1=Erdős|author1-link=Paul Erdős|first2=A.|last2=Rényi|author2-link=Alfréd Rényi|title=Asymmetric graphs|journal=[[Acta Mathematica Hungarica]]|volume=14|issue=3|year=1963|pages=295–315|doi=10.1007/BF01895716|doi-access=free}}.</ref>

==Trees==
The smallest asymmetric [[tree (graph theory)|tree]] has seven vertices: it consists of three paths of lengths 1, 2, and 3, linked at a common endpoint.<ref>{{citation|first=Louis V.|last=Quintas|title=Extrema concerning asymmetric graphs|journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]|volume=3|year=1967|pages=57–82|issue=1|doi=10.1016/S0021-9800(67)80018-8|doi-access=free}}.</ref> In contrast to the situation for graphs, almost all trees are symmetric. In particular, if a tree is chosen [[discrete uniform distribution|uniformly at random]] among all trees on ''n'' labeled nodes, then with [[probability]] tending to 1 as ''n'' increases, the tree will contain some two leaves adjacent to the same node and will have symmetries exchanging these two leaves.<ref name="er63"/>
